title: How do String and StringBuffer handle memory differently?
shortTitle: How do String and StringBuffer handle memory differently?
keyPoints: String: immutable, each modification creates a new object on the heap
StringBuilder/Buffer: mutable, modifies an internal array in place
StringBuilder starts with capacity 16, doubles when full
String concatenation in a loop creates N objects; StringBuilder creates 1
String objects eligible for String Pool sharing; StringBuilder is not pooled

s1_definition.oneliner: String creates a new object for every change. StringBuilder/Buffer modifies a resizable internal array in place, avoiding repeated allocation.
s1_definition.profdef:
Memory differences:

- **String:** New object per modification. `"a" + "b"` → new String("ab"). In a loop, N concatenations = N objects.
- **StringBuilder:** Modifies an internal char/byte array. Starts at capacity 16. Doubles when full. One object for all appends.
- **StringBuffer:** Same memory model as StringBuilder, with synchronized methods.
s1_definition.analogy: String: printing a new page every time you add a word. StringBuilder: writing on a notepad that grows when you reach the end. The notepad is reused; the printed pages are discarded.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  String: s += "x" × N
    → N new String objects → N garbage → GC pressure

  StringBuilder: sb.append("x") × N
    → 1 object, resizable array → minimal GC
    → capacity: 16 → 34 → 70 → 142 → ... (doubles)

  Pre-size: new StringBuilder(1024) → avoid resizing
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
String creates a new object for every modification. StringBuilder modifies an internal resizable array in place. In a loop, String concatenation creates N garbage objects while StringBuilder uses one. Pre-size StringBuilder to avoid resizing overhead.

One sentence to remember: String allocates per change, StringBuilder modifies in place – pre-size StringBuilder for best performance.
